## What was wrong

Newsletter sends in [newsletter.py](file:///workspace/shopkit/marketing/newsletter.py) only checked `marketing_opt_in`, so opted-in customers with badly typed addresses imported from the old system (which used the loose `isEmail` from [StringUtils.py](file:///workspace/shopkit/common/StringUtils.py) — just "has an @ after position 0 and some dot") were still emailed, causing bounces.

## The fix

The shop's own signup and checkout flows both validate with `is_valid_email` from shopkit/utils.validation` (its docstring: *"Pragmatic check used at signup and checkout"*). The newsletter now applies that same check:

```python
def recipients(customers: list[Customer]) -> list[Customer]:
    return [c for c in customers if c.marketing_opt_in and is_valid_email(c.email)]
```

Since [`batches()`](file:///workspace/shopkit/marketing/newsletter.py#L24-L25) is built on top of `recipients()`, the actual provider send path is covered by the one-line filter — every opted-in customer whose email fails the shop's check is skipped, no more. I also updated the module docstring to record the behavior.
